key_insight: How training data is ordered and grouped can materially change LLM training efficiency, even when the data itself stays the same. The paper shows that smart data organization can help models learn better in fewer epochs.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the underexplored problem of data organization in LLM training: beyond which samples to include, how should training data be arranged to improve efficiency and model quality when training for only one or a few epochs?
method: Reuses pre-computed sample-level scores to analyze how different data organization strategies affect training outcomes.
Systematically compares multiple ways of arranging training data rather than only changing the data selection set.
Evaluates how organization choices influence learning dynamics, efficiency, and final model performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that data pipeline design is not just an engineering detail but a lever for better and faster LLM training. It can help reduce wasted compute and improve results without needing new model architectures.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing the training pipeline with a highlighted data organization step
Side-by-side chart comparing different data ordering strategies and their training performance
Heatmap of sample-level scores mapped to training order
Icon-based illustration of compute savings and model improvement
paper_title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training
paper_authors: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang
